arxiv-2210-16986.title: A Practical Distributed ADMM Solver for Billion-Scale Generalized Assignment Problems Conference: Proceedings of the 31st ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management; October 17–21, 2022; Atlanta, GA, USA Proceedings of the 31st ACM International Conference on Information an
arxiv-2210-16986.creator: Jun Zhou, Feng Qi, Zhigang Hua, Daohong Jian, Ziqi Liu, Hua Wu, Xingwen Zhang, Shuang Yang
arxiv-2210-16986.description: Abstract . Assigning items to owners is a common problem found in various real-world applications, for example, audience-channel matching in marketing campaigns, borrower-lender matching in loan management, and shopper-merchant matching in e-commerce. Given an objective and multiple constraints, an assignment problem can be formulated as a constrained optimization problem.

arxiv-2301-08362.title: The Holographic Map of an Evaporating Black Hole
arxiv-2301-08362.creator: Zsolt Gyongyosi a , Timothy J. Hollowood a , S. Prem Kumar a , Andrea Legramandi a,b,c and Neil Talwar a
arxiv-2301-08362.description: Abstract We construct a holographic map that takes the semi-classical state of an evaporating black hole and its Hawking radiation to a microscopic model that reflects the scrambling dynamics of the black hole. The microscopic model is given by a nested sequence of random unitaries, each one implementing a scrambling time step of the black hole evolution.

arxiv-2306-17329.title: Kernel ϵ \epsilon -Greedy for Multi-Armed Bandits with Covariates
arxiv-2306-17329.creator: Sakshi Arya 1 and Bharath K. Sriperumbudur 2
arxiv-2306-17329.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Sakshi Arya 1 and Bharath K. Sriperumbudur 2. We consider the ϵ \epsilon -greedy strategy for the multi-arm bandit with covariates (MABC) problem, where the mean reward functions are assumed to lie in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS).

arxiv-2308-15707.title: Jet power extracted from ADAFs and the application to Fermi BL Lacertae objects 2023 Jet power extracted from ADAFs and the application to Fermi BL Lacertae objects – A
arxiv-2308-15707.creator: Yongyun Chen(陈永云), Qiusheng Gu(顾秋生), Junhui Fan(樊军辉), Xiaoling Yu (俞效龄), Nan Ding(丁楠), Xiaotong Guo (郭晓通), Dingrong Xiong(熊定荣)
arxiv-2308-15707.description: Abstract We calculate the jet power of the Blandford-Znajek (BZ) model and the hybrid model based on the self-similar solution of advection-dominated accretion flows (ADAFs). We study the formation mechanism of the jets of BL Lacs with known redshifts detected by the Fermi satellite after 10 yr of data (4FGL-DR2).

arxiv-2407-13617.title: Fast Scrambling at the Boundary
arxiv-2407-13617.creator: Ancel Larzul, Anirvan M. Sengupta, Antoine Georges, Marco Schirò
arxiv-2407-13617.description: Abstract Many-body systems which saturate the quantum bound on chaos are attracting interest across a wide range of fields. Notable examples include the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model and its variations, all characterised by some form or randomness and all to all couplings.

arxiv-2409-11239.title: LLM-as-a-Judge & Reward Model: What They Can and Cannot Do
arxiv-2409-11239.creator: Guijin Son, Hyunwoo Ko, Hoyoung Lee, Yewon Kim, Seunghyeok Hong, Yonsei University, OnelineAI, Hankuk University of Foreign Studies, Kangwon National University, The University of Suwon
arxiv-2409-11239.description: Abstract LLM-as-a-Judge and reward models are widely used alternatives of multiple-choice questions or human annotators for large language model (LLM) evaluation. Their efficacy shines in evaluating long-form responses, serving a critical role as evaluators of leaderboards and as proxies to align LLMs via reinforcement learning.

arxiv-2411-14969.title: Stabilization of macroscopic dynamics by fine-grained disorder in many-species ecosystems
arxiv-2411-14969.creator: Juan Giral Martínez, Silvia De Monte, Matthieu Barbier
arxiv-2411-14969.description: Abstract A central feature of complex systems is the relevance and entanglement of different levels of description. For instance, the dynamics of ecosystems can be alternatively described in terms of large ecological processes and classes of organisms, or of individual species and their relations.

arxiv-2504-00321.title: A Hybrid Systems Model of Feedback Optimization for Linear Systems: Convergence and Robustness
arxiv-2504-00321.creator: Oscar Jed R. Chuy, Matthew T. Hale, Ricardo G. Sanfelice
arxiv-2504-00321.description: Abstract Feedback optimization algorithms compute inputs to a system using real-time output measurements, which helps mitigate the effects of disturbances. However, existing work often models both system dynamics and computations in either discrete or continuous time, which may not accurately model some applications.

arxiv-2504-05270.title: Dirac particle in Newman-Unti-Tamburino spacetime
arxiv-2504-05270.creator: N.G. Krylova 1,2 , V.M. Red’kov 1 1 Institute of Physics, National Academy of Sciences of Belarus 2 Belarusian State Agrarian Technical University, Belarus
arxiv-2504-05270.description: Abstract Key Words : Riemannian geometry, Newman-Unti-Tamburino spacetime, Dirac equation, spin 1/2 particle, NUT charge We derive the Dirac equation for a particle in the background of the Newman-Unti-Tamburino (NUT) spacetime by applying the tetrad formalism, and separate the angular and radial parts.

arxiv-2505-05806.title: Image Segmentation via Variational Model Based Tailored UNet: A Deep Variational Framework
arxiv-2505-05806.creator: Kaili Qi, Wenli Yang, Ye Li, Zhongyi Huang
arxiv-2505-05806.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Kaili Qi, Wenli Yang, Ye Li, Zhongyi Huang. Traditional image segmentation methods, such as variational models based on partial differential equations (PDEs), offer strong mathematical interpretability and precise boundary modeling, but often suffer from sensitivity to parameter settings and high computational costs. In contrast, deep learning models such as UNet, which are relatively lightweight in parameters, excel in automatic feature extraction but lack theoretical interpretability and require extensive labeled data.

arxiv-2507-04869.title: Extension Operators for Fractional Sobolev Spaces on Lipschitz Submanifolds
arxiv-2507-04869.creator: Philipp Weder
arxiv-2507-04869.description: Abstract A well-known result is that any Lipschitz domain is an extension domain for W s , p W^{s,p} . This paper extends this result to Lipschitz subsets of compact Lipschitz submanifolds of ℝ n \mathbb{R}^{n} . We adapt the construction of an extension operator for Lipschitz domains in [ 1 ] to manifolds via local coordinate charts.

arxiv-2510-00304.title: Barriers for Learning in an Evolving World: Mathematical Understanding of Loss of Plasticity
arxiv-2510-00304.creator: Amir Joudaki, Giulia Lanzillotta, Mohammad Samragh Razlighi, Iman Mirzadeh, Keivan Alizadeh, Thomas Hofmann, Mehrdad Farajtabar, Fartash Faghri
arxiv-2510-00304.description: Abstract Deep learning models excel in stationary data but struggle in non-stationary environments due to a phenomenon known as loss of plasticity (LoP), the degradation of their ability to learn in the future. This work presents a first-principles investigation of LoP in gradient-based learning.

arxiv-2512-10556.title: A note on modular properties of non-principal and non-coprincipal admissible C 2 ( 1 ) C^{(1)}_{2} -modules of integer level
arxiv-2512-10556.creator: Minoru Wakimoto
arxiv-2512-10556.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Minoru Wakimoto. Abstract For the affine Lie algebra C_{2}^{(1)} we study non-principal and non-coprincipal admissible modules of integer level and their quantum Hamiltonian reduction, and show that they have \Gamma_{0}(2) -modular invariance. 1 Introduction Admissible representations are introduced in [ 4 ] as a class of irreducible highest weight modules of affine Lie algebras whose characters are modular functions, and are classified in [ 5 ] .

britannica-1911-malory-sir-thomas.description: Article 'Malory, Sir Thomas' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 17), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. famous English classic, the Morte d’Arthur. pmc-10690064.title: Nutritional Considerations in Colorectal Surgery in Diverting Ileostomy Patients: A Review
pmc-10690064.creator: Athanasios Migdanis, Ioannis Migdanis, Georgios D Koukoulis
pmc-10690064.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Colorectal surgery often results in a temporary or permanent ileostomy construction. The general nutritional status and intake of patients with an ileostomy have not received much attention and scientific evidence is lacking. Nutritional complications associated with ileostomy formation and colonic exclusion include fluid (dehydration) and electrolyte abnormalities (mainly hyponatremia), impaired renal function occurring from plasma volume depletion, and reduced energy absorption due to the role of the large bowel in energy assimilation.

pmc-10709285.title: Robust markers associated with floral traits in roses are suitable for marker-assisted selection across gene pools
pmc-10709285.creator: Dietmar Schulz, Marcus Linde, Thomas Debener
pmc-10709285.description: We investigated the potential of markers associated with floral traits for parental selection in a cut rose breeding program. We analysed six Kompetitive Allele Specific PCR (KASP) markers for three important floral traits, petal length, petal number and scent, derived from experiments in a garden rose population.

pmc-11327015.title: Comparative transcriptome analysis of resistant and susceptible watermelon genotypes reveals the role of RNAi, callose, proteinase, and cell wall in squash vein yellowing virus resistance
pmc-11327015.creator: Rahul Kumar, Bidisha Chanda, Scott Adkins, Chandrasekar S. Kousik
pmc-11327015.description: Watermelon (Citrullus lanatus) is the third largest fruit crop in the world in term of production. However, it is susceptible to several viruses. Watermelon vine decline (WVD), caused by whitefly-transmitted squash vein yellowing virus (SqVYV), is a disease that has caused over $60 million in losses in the US and continues to occur regularly in southeastern states.

pmc-11378932.title: The health legacy of coal mining: Analysis of mortality rates over time in England and Wales (1981–2019)
pmc-11378932.creator: Matthew Shaikh
pmc-11378932.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background– Coal mining areas in the UK continue to suffer worse health outcomes despite the industry disappearing by the early 1990s. Unemployment and deprivation are cited as key explanations. However, as the health effects of hazardous working environments continue after the industry's closure, it is unclear to what extent this ongoing health deficit is due to the legacy health effect of coal mining versus socioeconomic factors, including unemployment and deprivation.Methods– I isolate the legacy health effect of coal mining using a matching

pmc-11494254.title: Implementation of a Clinical Decision Support System for Antimicrobial Prescribing in Sub-Saharan Africa: Multisectoral Qualitative Study
pmc-11494254.creator: Nathan Peiffer-Smadja, Sophie Descousse, Elsa Courrèges, Audrey Nganbou, Pauline Jeanmougin, Gabriel Birgand, Séverin Lénaud, Anne-Lise Beaumont, Claire Durand, Tristan Delory, Josselin Le Bel, Elisabeth Bouvet, Sylvie Lariven, Eric D'Ortenzio, Issa Konaté, Marielle Karine Bouyou-Akotet, Abdoul-Sala
pmc-11494254.description: BackgroundSuboptimal use of antimicrobials is a driver of antimicrobial resistance in West Africa. Clinical decision support systems (CDSSs) can facilitate access to updated and reliable recommendations.ObjectiveThis study aimed to assess contextual factors that could facilitate the implementation of a CDSS for antimicrobial prescribing in West Africa and Central Africa and to identify tailored implementation strategies.

pmc-12118733.title: Some paradoxes and unresolved aspects of hepatic de novo lipogenesis
pmc-12118733.creator: John G. Jones
pmc-12118733.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Hepatic de novo lipogenesis (DNL) is a critical pathway in both liver intermediary metabolism and whole-body nutrient management. In the setting of excessive caloric intake, increased DNL fluxes are implicated in the pathogenesis of metabolic-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). As a result, there is intense interest both in the measurement of DNL activity and in gaining a better understanding on how this drives MASLD development. While much progress has been made towards these objectives, a number of intriguing uncertainties and paradoxes remain.

pmc-12469961.title: Quercetin and Its Structural Analogs as NUDT5 Inhibitors: A Preliminary In Silico Study
pmc-12469961.creator: Emilia Gligorić, Milica Vidić, Branislava Teofilović, Nevena Grujić-Letić, Sunil Gaikwad
pmc-12469961.description: Nucleotide diphosphate hydrolase type 5 (NUDT5) plays a significant role in the estrogen-signaling pathway and is overexpressed in breast cancer. This study aimed to explore the anti-breast cancer potential of quercetin and its 52 structural analogs by targeting the NUDT5 enzyme using the in silico molecular docking method.

pmc-12710605.title: Study of microstructure formation in epoxy based systems using small angle neutron scattering
pmc-12710605.creator: Natasha Shirshova, Leide P. Cavalcanti, Sarah Youngs, Valeria Arrighi
pmc-12710605.description: Structural/multifunctional electrolytes (SE) are an essential part of novel types of energy storage devices, structural supercapacitors and structural batteries. They are able to perform two functions simultaneously, conduct ions and withstand mechanical load. The most promising SEs consist of two independent phases, i.e. have a bicontinuous structure.

pmc-12986569.title: Kissing Bond Damage Identification and Evaluation in CFRP-Reinforced Steel Plates Using Mixed-Frequency Ultrasonic Guided Waves
pmc-12986569.creator: Ruiqi Guan, Haifeng Li, Weilong Ni, Tansheng Huang, Kai Wang, Xue Han
pmc-12986569.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). CFRP laminates are widely adopted for the strengthening of steel structures and the debonding damage poses a severe threat to the integrity of CFRP-reinforced structures. However, as the early stage of debonding damage, kissing bond detection in these structures using the conventional ultrasonic guided waves method is a significant challenge due to the imperceptibility of microscale damage and the complexity of the wave properties at the interface.

pmc-13184412.title: Microcirculatory perfusion is improved with plasma, but not with crystalloids, in a rat polytraumatic shock model
pmc-13184412.creator: Tarık Gözden, Bulent Ergin, Can Ince, Nicole P. Juffermans
pmc-13184412.description: BackgroundTraumatic shock is associated with microcirculatory dysfunction. Plasma resuscitation for traumatic shock outside the context of bleeding may exert benefit by augmenting intravascular volume and inhibiting endotheliopathy. However, its effects on microcirculatory perfusion and tissue oxygenation in trauma remain poorly understood.

pmc-13445926.title: Evaluating progestin-primed and GnRH antagonist ovarian stimulation protocols in PGT-A cycles: implications for clinical practice
pmc-13445926.creator: Burak Elmas, Ozge Karaosmanoglu, Aysen Yuceturk, Ilke Ozer Aslan, Burcu Aksu Turan, Nuri Peker, Omur Albayrak, Hakan Berkil, Bulent Tiras
pmc-13445926.description: BackgroundProgestin-primed ovarian stimulation (PPOS) has emerged as an alternative to GnRH-antagonist protocols in IVF, yet its impact on embryo chromosomal competence remains controversial. Evidence is particularly limited regarding whether PPOS influences blastocyst euploidy rates and key clinical outcomes in PGT-A cycles, and whether these effects vary according to maternal age and ovarian reserve status.

pmc-13682091.title: Kinematics and muscle activation of the lower limb during barefoot and flip-flop running
pmc-13682091.creator: Chun Wai Wong, Chia-Ming Chang, Ying-Che Tseng, Chih-Wei Chen, Hsiu-Chen Lin
pmc-13682091.description: BackgroundFlip-flop and barefoot running are increasingly common; however, their biomechanical effects remain unclear. This study examined lower-limb kinematics and muscle activation during treadmill running under barefoot, conventional flip-flop, Y-Sandal, and shod conditions.MethodsSixteen volunteers were recruited to run on a treadmill under four footwear conditions at three speeds.
